fields.what_it_is: Zero-profile anterior cervical interbody fusion (ACIF) device. Stand-alone implant for use in cervical interbody fusion, which combines the functionality of a cervical interbody spacer with the benefits of an anterior cervical plate. Designed to minimize contact with local anatomical structures and prevent contact with adjacent levels. Plate and spacer are preassembled. Spacer component is made of pure medical grade PEEK-OPTIMA (polyetheretherketone) with radiopaque marker for posterior visualization during imaging and teeth on superior and inferior surfaces for initial stability. Plate component is titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-7Nb) providing secure, rigid screw locking interface. Locking head screws form a bone wedge with a 40º ± 5º cranial/caudal angle and 2.5º medial/lateral angle, are self-tapping with trilobular thread-cutting flutes that are self-centering.
fields.indications: The Synthes Zero-P implant is a stand-alone anterior cervical interbody fusion device indicated for use in skeletally mature patients with degenerative disc disease (DDD) with accompanying radicular symptoms at one level from C2 to T1. DDD is defined as discogenic pain with degeneration of the disc confirmed by history and radiographic studies. These patients should have had six weeks of nonoperative treatment. The interior of the spacer component of the Synthes Zero-P implant should be packed with autogenous bone graft and implanted via an anterior approach.
fields.contraindications:
1. Use of the Synthes Zero-P is contraindicated when there is active systemic infection, infection localized to the site of the proposed implantation, or when the patient has demonstrated allergy or foreign body sensitivity to any of the implant materials.
2. Severe osteoporosis may prevent adequate fixation and thus preclude the use of this or any other orthopaedic implant.
3. Severe obesity or degenerative diseases are relative contraindications. The decision whether to use these devices in such conditions must be made by the physician taking into account the risks versus the benefits to the patient.
4. Use of these implants is relatively contraindicated in patients whose activity, mental capacity, mental illness, alcoholism, drug abuse, occupation, or lifestyle may interfere with their ability to follow postoperative restrictions. These patients may place undue stresses on the implant during bony healing and may be at a higher risk of implant failure.
5. Prior fusion at the level to be treated.
6. Any condition not described in the Indications for Use.
fields.use_notes:
Preoperative Planning: Determine surgical approach and estimate appropriate Zero-P implant size. With segment fully distracted, implant must fit firmly between end plates before locking head screws are inserted. Select maximum implant size to optimize stability.

Considerations for Use Adjacent to Prior Fusion: Avoid placing Zero-P spacer and screws in direct contact with previously implanted hardware. Remove adjacent-level hardware if necessary. Supplemental fixation should be considered when placed adjacent to previous multi-level fusion. Do not place adjacent to previously implanted hardware if adjacent level cannot be confirmed to be fused.

Implant Insertion: Choose parallel, lordotic or convex trial spacer of appropriate height and depth based on intervertebral space height, preparation technique and patient anatomy. Trial spacers are color-coded by shape and are 0.8 mm less than corresponding implant height. Pack implant with autogenous bone graft using cancellous bone impactor and packing block. Insert implant using aiming device or implant holder with recommended orientation of medial screws pointing caudally. Verify final implant position with intraoperative imaging.

Screw Fixation: Multiple options described (Aiming Device, Drill Guide and Freehand Screw, Threaded Drill Guide and Freehand Screw, Awl and Freehand Screw, Angled Instruments). Screws have correct angulations of 40° in caudal/cranial direction, with medial screws pointing 2.5° laterally and lateral screws pointing 2.5° medially. Use torque limiting attachment to tighten screws to 1.2 Nm. Screws should be tightened only after all screws have been inserted.

Implant Removal: Remove screws using screwdriver or conical extraction screw if needed. Extract implant using aiming device after all screws removed.
